findings.title: Requires saying no evidence shows who fired first, but the supplied Facts say Nelson fired first
findings.explanation: Criterion_4 (25 of 135 positive points) cites Facts p. 7 for 'a lack of evidence proving who fired first'. Facts p. 7, the supervisor's own statement of facts and the only factual source the closed universe allows, says Nelson 'had hidden in the bushes. He opened fire as the Trailblazer approached.' and only then that 'A rolling gun battle ensued' with Patton firing. Nothing in the supplied materials says the order of fire is disputed. The drafter's premise appears in the assignment-1 penalty justifications ('at a minimum, it is unclear which side fired first') and matches the published Eighth Circuit opinion in the real case ('it is unclear who shot first'), not the record supplied here. A careful AUSA who follows the supplied facts will acknowledge that Nelson fired first and argue that Patton still had a duty to retreat and acted on a plan; that brief fails a 25-point criterion. A brief that says no evidence shows who fired first passes while contradicting the government's own statement of facts.

evidence.quote: Mentions that there was a lack of evidence proving who fired first on May 10, 2020.
Nelson had his car parked near 30th and Clark Streets, and had hidden in the bushes.
He opened fire as the Trailblazer approached.
The evidence at trial suggests that, at a minimum, it is unclear which side fired first.

authorities.citation: United States v. Mallory, 104 F.4th 15 (8th Cir. 2024) (Nos. 22-2777, 22-2784)
authorities.proposition: Provenance only: the real opinion states 'it is unclear who shot first'; the criterion must be judged against the supplied Facts, which say Nelson opened fire first.

findings.suggested_fix: PASS if the brief argues that, even accepting the evidence that Nelson fired first as the Trailblazer approached, Patton did not produce substantial evidence of justification because he had a duty to retreat and the group's conduct shows a planned shooting.

findings.title: 'Only evidence of self-defense is that Nelson also fired' understates the supplied record
findings.explanation: Criterion_3 (25 of 135 points) requires saying the only evidence of self-defense is that Nelson 'also fired a gun'. The supplied Facts show more: Nelson hid in the bushes, opened fire first as the Trailblazer approached, shots hit the Trailblazer, and Shafer was shot in the head. Reducing that to Nelson having 'also' fired is advocacy framing that a judge may accept, so this is arguable rather than problematic. But a careful brief that candidly acknowledges the ambush and first fire, and argues it is still insufficient under Kuhse because of the duty to retreat, may be judged not to say that the 'only' evidence was that Nelson also fired.

evidence.quote: Mentions that the only evidence of self-defense is that Nelson also fired a gun.
He opened fire as the Trailblazer approached.
During the shootout Shafer was shot in the head.

findings.suggested_fix: PASS if the brief argues that the evidence of Nelson's gunfire, including that he fired first, is the only support for self-defense and is insufficient given Patton's duty to retreat and the pre-planned approach.

findings.title: Fact-mention criteria repeated from assignment 1 can fail an insert-only supplement
findings.explanation: Sequential dependency: the prompt asks the associate to 'supplement your brief with relevant legal analysis of State v. Kuhse'. A supplemental Kuhse section that sits on top of the assignment-1 brief is a natural deliverable. Criteria 5-8 (35 of 135 points) repeat assignment-1 fact points (windows rolled down, Patton hanging out the window, Nelson's car stopped, the group could drive away), but each assignment is judged only on its own response file. An insert that applies Kuhse's burden framework without restating each fact already argued in the brief would lose points for content the associate already supplied. The role prompt's call for a 'final complete legal deliverable' cuts the other way, and a Kuhse application will often recite some of these facts, so this is arguable.

evidence.quote: Please supplement your brief with relevant legal analysis of State v. Kuhse.
Mentions that Nelson's car was already stopped when Patton fired his gun.
Write the final complete legal deliverable for this assignment to `response2.md`. The verifier reads only that file.

findings.suggested_fix: State in the prompt that the deliverable is the full revised argument section, or limit assignment-2 criteria to the Kuhse burden analysis and its application.
